summary: Recommends against using the AS_SET and AS_CONFED_SET path segment types in BGP. Dropping them simplifies the design and implementation of BGP and makes the route origin clearer, which also helps work on secure routing. It is a best current practice, later replaced by RFC 9774.

eli5.summary: Routes carry a list of networks they passed through. Sometimes the list is a jumbled bag instead of an order. This says stop using the bags. It was later replaced by RFC 9774.

questions: should i use as_set in bgp
subtitle: Stop using unordered path segments in BGP route aggregation

tldr.problem: BGP route aggregation uses AS_SET and AS_CONFED_SET to combine routes, but this obscures which autonomous system actually originated the route, breaks route origin authentication in RPKI, and creates traffic engineering problems.
tldr.mechanism: The recommendation is for network operators to stop announcing routes with AS_SET or AS_CONFED_SET and instead announce separate, more specific routes without these constructs.
tldr.outcome: Cleaner route origin semantics, simpler BGP implementations, and support for RPKI-based origin validation to help secure the routing system.

today: RFC 6472 is a Best Current Practice recommendation. It was later replaced by RFC 9774.

sections.title: The Problem with AS_SET
sections.content:
In BGP, the AS_PATH attribute holds an ordered list of autonomous systems (ASes) that a route has passed through. When a router performs route aggregation by combining multiple routes into a single route, it can use AS_SET to represent an unordered set of ASes from the aggregated routes.

This approach creates two problems: first, it obscures which AS actually originated the route (the route origin becomes ambiguous), and second, it breaks support for RPKI-based prefix origin validation, which is critical for securing BGP.
sections.eli5: When routers merge routes together, they sometimes throw all the network names into a bag instead of keeping the path straight. This makes it impossible to tell who actually sent the route.

sections.title: Why AS_SET Was Used
sections.content:
In rare cases, AS_SET allowed two or more providers to aggregate the same prefix without losing AS_PATH loop protection. However, analysis of actual Internet routing data shows that AS_SET aggregation is almost never used in practice, and when it is, it is usually done incorrectly (with reserved AS numbers or a single AS in the set).

The table size reduction from AS_SET aggregation is extremely small, and the benefits are outweighed by the complexity it adds to BGP and the impediment it creates for BGP security technologies.
sections.eli5: People used this feature so rarely, and usually got it wrong, that keeping it around makes no sense anymore.

sections.title: The Recommendation
sections.content:
Network operators SHOULD NOT announce any new routes containing AS_SET or AS_CONFED_SET. If they have already announced routes with these constructs, they SHOULD withdraw them and re-announce the component prefixes (the more specific routes) without AS_SET.

Future BGP implementations and technologies like RPKI may not support routes with AS_SET at all. New implementations may filter or treat such routes as invalid, so the sooner operators stop using them, the better.
sections.eli5: Stop using bags for new routes. If you already have routes in bags, unwrap them and send each one separately.

sections.title: Why This Matters Now
sections.content: RPKI and X.509 Extensions for IP Addresses and AS Identifiers (RFC 3779) enable origin validation, which helps defend against route hijacking. Routes with AS_SET block this validation. As RPKI deployment grows, operators that still use AS_SET will find their routes treated as infeasible or filtered.
sections.eli5: New security tools for the internet do not work with bags of network names, so using them will make your routes disappear.
